header.title: Shift to low-cost autonomous/attritable systems favors defense-tech startups and software layer

s01_bottom_line.text: Funding for defense-tech startups focused on autonomous systems, unmanned platforms and defense software has hit records ($14.6bn US through May 2026; $8.7bn Europe in 2025), with Anduril ($61bn valuation) and Palantir able to act as primes, as militaries move to low-cost attritable systems and a critical AI software layer.

The article argues winners will be firms addressing specific production constraints (components, processes, software, enabling infrastructure) rather than broad themes, and that investors must separate pilots from repeat orders.

A durable reorientation toward autonomous mass and software could shift share toward new entrants and the software layer, but most leading names (Anduril, Helsing) are private, and the article does not establish which listed companies capture the economics.
